headline: Reserve charge hits underwriting, buybacks step up

kpis.label: Net operating income per diluted share

summary_short: Net income was $233M, or $6.12 per share, and net operating income was $290M, or $7.62 per share. Core combined ratio was 105.8% after about $268M of unfavorable prior-year reserve development.
summary_long: Core gross written premium fell 4.0% to $3.7B, with Reinsurance Treaty down 6.2% and Global Wholesale & Specialty up 3.2%. Net investment income rose to $634M on higher alternative investment returns. Everest repurchased $474M of shares in the quarter. Book value per share was $381.04, or $414.00 excluding unrealized losses on fixed maturities. Pre-tax underwriting loss was $223M for the Group.
confidence_notes: Net operating income is non-GAAP. Deltas computed from the release's year-ago figures. The reserve charge added 8.5 points to the Group combined ratio.

drivers.explanation: Net unfavorable prior-year reserve development of about $268M, from strengthened casualty reinsurance reserves, added 8.5 points to the Group combined ratio.
Driven by higher alternative investment returns.
Reinsurance Treaty premiums fell 6.2% as the team stays disciplined through the market cycle; Global Wholesale & Specialty grew 3.2%.
CEO cites strengthened balance sheet, accelerated capital return and share repurchases as a top priority.
